draft.title: Lenz's law
card: When the magnetic flux through a coil changes, a current is induced in the coil. Lenz's law gives the direction of that current.
The induced current flows in the direction that opposes the change in flux that caused it. It opposes the change, not the flux itself.

If the flux through a coil is increasing, the induced current makes a field that points opposite to the original field. If the flux is decreasing, it makes a field that points the same way, to try to keep the flux up.

This follows from conservation of energy. If the induced current helped the change, the change would grow on its own and energy would appear from nothing. Instead, work must be done to move a magnet against the coil, and that work becomes electrical energy.
draft.remember: The induced current fights the change in flux, because anything else would create energy from nothing.

a.q: The north pole of a bar magnet is pushed towards a coil. What does the induced current in the coil do?
opts: Makes a field that opposes the increase in flux
Makes a field that adds to the magnet's field
Flows only after the magnet stops moving
Makes a field that cancels the magnet's field everywhere
a.why: Pushing the magnet in increases the flux, so the induced current makes a field that opposes that increase. The second option is tempting, but a field that added to the change would make the flux grow even faster, which would create energy from nothing.
a.clue: The current acts against the change that causes it.

b.q: A magnet is pulled away from a coil at constant speed. Why must the person pulling do work, according to Lenz's law?
opts: The induced current opposes the change, so it resists the pull
The induced current helps the change, so it assists the pull
The magnet loses its magnetism as it leaves the coil
The coil's flux stays constant, so energy is stored in it
b.why: Pulling the magnet away decreases the flux. The induced current opposes this decrease, so the coil pulls back on the magnet and work must be done against it. That work supplies the electrical energy. The assisting option is wrong because it would speed the magnet up and create energy from nothing.
b.clue: Think about where the electrical energy comes from.
